mappedContracts.statement: The first Codex execution is planning-only. It may create or update programme-governance artefacts, Conductor context, the canonical contract, GitHub issues/subissues, and the planning PR, but it must not change runtime source, dependencies, lockfiles, release configuration, or live Substack state.
acceptanceCriteria: The planning PR contains no runtime feature implementation or dependency migration.
Codex stops after the planning PR is pushed and all available checks are green or a pre-existing check failure is precisely evidenced.
The final planning-stage report explicitly states that implementation has not started.
requiredEvidence: GitHub Actions check URLs and conclusions

mappedContracts.statement: Represent the programme as a native GitHub issue hierarchy cross-referenced bidirectionally with Conductor.
acceptanceCriteria: One programme issue contains native phase subissues.
Each phase issue contains native track subissues.
Every track contains native task subissues for all independently verifiable tasks.
Existing issues are reused rather than duplicated and are attached to the correct parent hierarchy.
Every Conductor phase, track, and task includes the corresponding GitHub issue number and URL; every issue includes the Conductor ID and path.
requiredEvidence: GitHub Project view or reproducible project configuration

mappedContracts.statement: Reconcile all existing issues, pull requests, branches, tracks, decisions, and partially implemented work before creating new work items.
acceptanceCriteria: Open issues #161 through #167 are mapped and reused.
Closed issue #168 and its implementation are explicitly audited against the new mutation contracts.
Open PR #176 is assessed and either incorporated, superseded with explanation, or retained with a documented dependency.
No duplicate issue or track is created for work already represented.
requiredEvidence: Issue and PR comments documenting supersession or reuse
